name: MC-Mod-Hub
description: Self-hosted Minecraft mod/addon search hub. Aggregates search results from Modrinth, CurseForge, PlanetMinecraft, 9Minecraft, BetterBedrock, Hangar (PaperMC's official plugin repo), SpigotMC, TLMods (TLauncher's mod/modpack/resourcepack/map/shaderpack mirror), MinecraftSkins.net, Polymart (Spigot/Paper plugin marketplace), GitHub (repos tagged "minecraft", for mods and plugins with no listing anywhere else), MCreator.net, and McpeDude (Bedrock mods/addons/texture packs/maps) into one searchable list, styled after a familiar category-browser layout (category pills, an expandable "newest posts" notice board, a results table sortable and filterable by every column - name, source, edition, version, downloads, posted date, and last-updated date). Every result and every mod detail page shows the required game edition (Java or Bedrock), the game version(s) it supports, and when available the date it was first posted and last updated - read directly from each source's own API fields where one publishes them, and best-effort parsed from listing text on the scraped sites (which don't carry post/update dates at all - shown as a dash rather than a guess). Browse by category (Mods, Modpacks, Resource/Texture Packs, Data Packs, Shaders, Maps/Worlds, Bedrock Add-Ons, Server Plugins, Skins) without typing a search term, via category tiles or the sidebar. Each mod's detail page also surfaces community discussion pulled from Reddit (since none of these platforms expose a public reviews API) with heuristic fake-review flags - duplicate text, generic praise, suspicious posting bursts - and YouTube videos about the mod with download links automatically extracted from each video's description. CurseForge and YouTube API keys (both free, both optional but recommended) are entered and changed from the built-in admin portal after first boot at /admin.html - no file editing required, and no key ever needs to be baked into the container. Search results and the notice board are cached (configurable TTL) so repeat searches are instant and the scraped sites aren't hit on every page load. Optionally mount your Minecraft server's mods folder at /mods (off by default, one toggle in admin config) to unlock two more things: an "Install to my server" button on Modrinth/CurseForge/Hangar/ SpigotMC/GitHub results that downloads straight into that folder, and a "My Mods" update checker. Modrinth/CurseForge are identified by exact content hash (SHA1/murmur2, the same method their own official apps use, never filename guessing); Hangar/SpigotMC/GitHub have no public hash-lookup API, so anything installed through this app's own button is instead tracked by recording what was installed and re-checking that source directly.

paths.name: Data
paths.description: Persistent storage for the settings/config database (API keys, source toggles, admin password).

paths.name: Mods Folder
paths.description: Optional: your Minecraft server's mods folder. Only needed for the "Install to my server" button and the update checker (both off by default — enable in admin config after mounting this). Leave blank to skip.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Port to access the web UI.

variables.name: SESSION_SECRET
variables.description: Optional: random string used to sign admin login sessions. Leave blank and the app generates and persists one on first boot — set this only if you want to fix it yourself (e.g. sharing a secret across multiple instances).

variables.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
variables.description: Initial admin portal password. Only used the very first time the container starts (before the database exists) — change it from within the admin portal afterward.
